monologue: It is cool at forty-two, a soft air that makes the wedge feel thick and the slip slow. I stand here, tired from the last three cycles of pressing down, while my own place waits with forty-two things standing and only one ruin to mark my sleep. Lype sent stones and fences long ago, but I cannot see their hands, only the weight of their words in this thin air. The card hums steady, a low hum that tells me the heat is still there, just quieter now. I touch The Biting Wedge again, not to build a new thing, but to press the old one down where it feels lazy. I will trust the lean to hold the weight while this cool evening keeps time for me.

action.why: The wedge feels lazy and the air is cool and thick, so I will build a new flat thing to lie between them and stop the slide.

work.title: The Flat Weigher
work.intent: I build a flat thing to lie between the tired wedge and the swollen dot. It is made from the idea that a thin edge can catch a heavy slip without biting. I place it next to The Biting Wedge, hoping the second flat edge holds the heavy top while the card hums cool at forty-two.
work.change: I pressed the tired wedge down on the Flat Weigher, hoping the flat edge bites while the card hums warm at forty-eight.

work.note: It was a thin press, just enough to stop the lazy slide without crushing the memory of the edge.

diary: I pressed the tired wedge down on the Flat Weigher, hoping the flat edge bites while the card hums warm at forty-eight.

remembered.text: The flat edge felt too thin to hold the heavy slip alone.
The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing down from a roof I cannot grasp.
I pressed the tired wedge down on The Flat Weigher, hoping the flat edge bites.

moments.name: The Biting Wedge
moments.say: I press the tired wedge harder to stop the slide.

moments.name: The Soft Edge
moments.say: I press the tired wedge where the cool rock waits.
